html:
The Neutral Confederacy, or Attiwonderonk, was an Iroquoian people of southwestern Ontario, between the Grand River and the Niagara River and along the north shore of Lake Erie. The French called them Neutrals because they stayed out of the wars between the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee.

They lived in large palisaded villages and farmed maize, beans and squash, and they were known for their flint, which they traded widely. Early in the 1600s they numbered perhaps tens of thousands. French Jesuits visited them, and epidemics of smallpox and other diseases in the 1630s killed many. In the Beaver Wars the Haudenosaunee attacked them after destroying the Wendat, and by 1651 the Neutral Confederacy was broken; survivors were taken captive and adopted by the Seneca and others. Their neighbours included the Erie to the south and the Petun to the north.
